title: Tunisia: Libya coach Youssef Dabo describes "wounded" opponent
text:

 Hossam Ahmed · Nov 16, 2026 Libya head coach Youssef Dabo spoke ahead of the crucial AFCON 2027 qualifier against Tunisia - Photo credit: المنتخب الليبي - Libyan National Team/Facebook Libya head coach Youssoupha Dabo has expressed readiness ahead of his side’s crucial Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) 2027 Matchday 4 qualifier against Tunisia, set to take place on Tuesday, November 17, at the June 11 Stadium in Tripoli. 
 Riding the momentum of a 2–0 away victory over the Carthage Eagles just days ago at the Taieb Mhiri Stadium in Sfax, Dabo noted that the squad's preparations have progressed seamlessly, continuing the high standards set from the start of the training camp.

 He pointed out that the current group of players is far more competitive than the squad he had at his disposal back in September, which gives him confidence that Libya has the necessary tools to back up their Sfax triumph—even while acknowledging that the return leg in front of home supporters will be an even tougher test.
 Despite holding the upper hand from the first meeting, Dabo warned about the opponent, describing Tunisia as a "wounded" opponent that still possesses significant quality and will arrive in Tripoli with a fierce determination to respond. 
 To counter this, the coach emphasized that Libya's primary objective will be establishing greater control over the rhythm of the game. 
 Hinting at tactical adjustments, Dabo revealed that he plans to alter the team's structural organization for the match, referencing past setups where Libya utilized a three-man backline—both against Botswana and during the closing stages of the victory in Sfax—as a genuine tactical option to neutralize Tunisia's expected approach.
 Addressing team news, Dabo brushed aside concerns over the absence of suspended team captain Hamdou Elhouni, stressing that the collective strength of his 24-man roster ensures every player is prepared and capable of stepping into the starting lineup. 
 Ultimately, the coach underscored the hunger within the dressing room to secure another win. While he noted that Tuesday's clash is not mathematically decisive on its own, he highlighted its vital strategic importance in putting Libya in a commanding position ahead of the final two qualifying matches scheduled for March.
